items.q: Contact lens overwearer with painful grey corneal infiltrate and hypopyon needs what first?
o: Corneal scraping for stains and culture then fortified antibiotics
items.exp: Microbial keratitis needs organism identification before intensive therapy; steroids alone melt infected corneas and patching incubates Pseudomonas. Small peripheral lesions may start fluoroquinolone monotherapy locally.
r: Incorrect. Graft follows perforation or scarring.
items.kp: Grey lens ulcer with pus level: scrape, then fortify.

items.q: Dry raised ulcer with feathery margins and satellite lesions after vegetative eye injury suggests what?
o: Fungal keratitis needing KOH and natamycin
items.exp: Filamentous fungi implant with plant matter, resist antibacterials and penetrate deep; prolonged antifungals with debridement cure, steroids contraindicated. Hypopyon here may harbour hyphae.
items.kp: Plant scratch ulcer ignoring drops: think fungus.

items.q: Soft lens wearer rinsing lenses in tap water with pain far exceeding signs and ring infiltrate most likely has what?
o: Acanthamoeba keratitis treated with biguanides for months
items.exp: Acanthamoeba tracks corneal nerves (radial perineuritis) causing agony with modest early signs; cysts resist therapy demanding months of PHMB or chlorhexidine with diamidines and pain control.
r: Incorrect. Bacteria match signs to pain.
items.kp: Tap water lenses plus agony plus ring: acanthamoeba.

items.q: Branching corneal ulcer with terminal bulbs staining fluorescein is diagnostic of what?
items.exp: Viral replication tracks epithelium in dendrites; topical or oral antivirals heal while steroids alone elongate ulcers into geographic blight. Reduced sensation and recurrences confirm herpetic habit.

items.q: Vesicles on the nasal tip in shingles warn of ocular involvement because which nerve is affected?
o: Nasociliary branch of ophthalmic division (Hutchinson sign)
items.exp: Nasal tip shares nasociliary supply with globe; Hutchinson predicts keratitis, uveitis and neuralgia needing urgent systemic antivirals and eye review. Delay risks scarring and chronic pain.
items.kp: Nose tip blisters: eye follows via nasociliary.

items.q: Descemetocele differs from perforated ulcer by which bedside findings?
o: Transparent herniating Descemet with formed chamber and negative Seidel versus flat chamber with leaking fluorescein
items.exp: Descemet bulges clear before rupture (impending perforation needing glue or patch graft urgently); perforation shallows the chamber with aqueous leak diluting fluorescein (Seidel). Both are surgical urgencies.
r: Incorrect. Chamber and leak separate them.
Correct. Bulge formed versus flat leaking.
items.kp: Clear bulge formed chamber: descemetocele about to burst.

items.q: Khodadoust line on a corneal graft with redness and vision drop signifies what and treatment?
o: Endothelial rejection needing intensive topical and systemic steroids
items.exp: Leukocyte line marches on endothelium in immune rejection; hourly steroids rescue clarity while infection instead shows infiltrate with discharge. Irreversible rejection re grafts.
items.kp: Line on graft with red eye: reject rejection with steroids.

items.q: Nummular subepithelial infiltrates with glare months after red eye epidemic are sequelae of what?
items.exp: Adenovirus leaves immune stromal dots scattering light; lubricants and brief cautious steroids ease visually significant cases while reassuring resolution over months.
items.kp: Epidemic red eye then dots and glare: adenovirus.

items.q: Pseudomonas corneal ulcer in lens wearers is feared chiefly because what?
o: Rapid stromal melting and perforation within hours needing admission
items.exp: Proteases liquefy collagen overnight with greenish mucopurulent discharge; hourly fortified therapy with admission and lens case culture controls damage. Delay perforates.

items.q: Steroids are contraindicated as solo therapy in which corneal infections?
o: Active bacterial, fungal, acanthamoeba and herpetic epithelial disease
items.exp: Steroids blunt immunity letting organisms replicate while masking signs; they enter only with antimicrobial cover for stromal inflammation or graft rejection. Solo use perforates infected corneas.
r: Correct. Never solo in live infection.
Incorrect. Dry eye uses mild steroids.
items.kp: Live corneal infection plus lone steroid equals perforation.
